### 9.3 The comparison is a natural transformation, and that is the form a consumer substitutes

`divFamZarToAffVehicle` (ADDENDUM 6) was componentwise: it said the two carriers agree at each
affine open. That is not what a consumer holding a section over a general test wants. It wants to
replace `divFunctor` by `divFunctorAff` and **keep its restriction equations** — which is
naturality, and which is what `divFunctorToAff` now provides.

The proof needs no gluing: the componentwise image of the chart-typed glued value already has the
*widened* pullback property, because `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` turns each clause of the
chart-typed `mapVal_spec` into the corresponding widened clause, and widened uniqueness
(`divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_of`) closes it.

Direction: **old → new only**, and that is content, not omission. By ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4
§4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can
confine, so no transformation back can exist.

### 9.4 What the R2 lane owes after this

**One item, and it is unchanged since ADDENDUM 5:** the **subordinate Stacks `0B8B` input** —
an affine open `W ⊇ supp d` lying inside one member of `d.cover`. I-0492 clause 2 says USE it, do
not re-derive it; mathlib has no form of `0B8B` and this tree constructs no curve but `P¹`.

**And one item that is NOT an obligation but is the lane's real exposure, stated because a green
build hides it.** Measured at this session's HEAD, with the substring collision against the
chart-typed `divFamZarAffineEquiv` excluded:

summary: "CORRECTED 2026-07-25 AFTER REVIEW (work-reviewer, I-0340). The original\
  \ claim on this leaf — that
(c2)/(c3)/(c4) become FREE for a swallow-or-miss adaptation\
  \ — is WRONG, and the reason is worth
knowing before anyone re-derives it.

\
  WHY \"FREE\" IS FALSE. `A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i` holds by `rfl` (proof\
  \ irrelevance makes
inf_le_left and inf_le_right the same proof at pieces i inf\
  \ pieces i), so EVERY DIAGONAL COMPONENT of
deltaLeft - deltaRight is identically\
  \ zero, for every adaptation. Hence coker(delta) always retains
prod_i ovlColength\
  \ i i iso prod_i colength i as a direct factor, and therefore

  clause (c4) \
  \ ==>  Module.Flat R (A.colength i) for every i.

(c4) can never be discharged\
  \ without flatness of the colengths. The off-diagonal image is the
ANTI-DIAGONAL\
  \ {(c, -c)}, not the whole off-diagonal block, so one copy of the overlap colength
\
  survives in the cokernel too.

THE CORRECT, STILL-VALUABLE CLAIM. For a swallow-or-miss\
  \ adaptation the surviving factors are
exactly: the colengths themselves, and one\
  \ leftover overlap colength isomorphic to them. All are
finite PROJECTIVE by (c1)\
  \ once the fibrewise-regularity input is supplied
(projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField),\
  \ hence flat. So

  (c2)/(c3)/(c4) REDUCE TO (c1)-projectivity plus the constant-rank/degree\
  \ input hdeg.

That is a genuine reduction — it removes the relative-flatness-over-a-nonreduced-base\
  \ content that
away-kerspan was stuck on — but it is a reduction, not a retirement.\
  \ away-kerspan stays blocked
rather than rejected for exactly this reason.

\
  THE ONE TECHNICAL LEMMA STILL NEEDED (unchanged): colength is invariant under shrinking\
  \ a piece to a
smaller open that still contains the trace, so the colength and\
  \ overlap-colength modules of the
swallowing pieces are identified. Ring-level\
  \ core: if V(g) cap V(h) = empty then h is a UNIT mod (g)
(1 lies in span{g,h}),\
  \ so Gamma(V)/(g) iso Gamma(V)_h/(g) = Gamma(D(h))/(g) via
IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen.\
  \ Watch the Opens-level `inf` bookkeeping — pieces i inf pieces j
is not syntactically\
  \ symmetric in i and j.
"
